title: The Iron Hunt
author: Jared Woodward
desc:
The purpose of this program is simple: carve muscle into strength with intention, discipline, and honesty. Every session follows the RPE system so you always know exactly how hard you should be pushing. The 8–10 RPE range is your highest intensity — no more than two reps in reserve, the zone where the weight feels heavy, the breath shortens, and the warrior inside you steps forward. The 6–8 RPE range keeps the body moving between those battles, emphasizing clean movement, steady tempo, and technical control. Lower intensities are not “exercises off or rests”; they’re designed to build quality movements, sharpening your form so the high‑intensity sets hit harder.

This program runs on a 3‑days‑on, 1‑day‑active‑recovery rhythm for twelve full weeks. The first phase builds hypertrophy with normal tempo work, expanding muscle fiber and preparing your frame for heavier demands. As the weeks progress, rep ranges shift toward strength, still with normal tempo, but with a growing emphasis on load, stability, and power. It’s a long march toward the Winter Forge Bulk — a season where strength becomes mass and mass becomes armor. This program is the sharpening stone before the cold.

Recovery is not optional. It is part of the work. You know what recovery stretches and movements work best for you. Listen to your body, take advantage of the active recovery days, and treat them as strategic resets rather than breaks. A warrior who ignores recovery becomes a ghost before the battle even begins. When soreness spikes, mobility slows, or fatigue creeps in take the rest. It will keep you in the fight.

Form is your shield. Control every rep, every tempo, every setup. Nothing ends a program faster than injury, and nothing builds strength faster than consistent, clean movement. Be honest with yourself — if a set felt too light, it didn’t count, and if you aren’t hitting the desired rep range, the work isn’t landing where it should. Going too heavy with sloppy form is just as bad; a warrior who chases weight instead of mastery becomes prey to the very iron he tries to conquer. If you had more in reserve than the RPE called for, adjust. Only warmup sets are allowed to be easy, and those are clearly marked. The rest demand truth, discipline, and the kind of control that keeps you in the hunt rather than broken on the battlefield.

Progressive overload is the backbone of your transformation. Add weight, add reps, add volume, add distance — every session should surpass the last time you completed that workout. This applies to both lifting and cardio. If a machine is taken or time is short, substitute intelligently: same muscle group, same intent, same effort. Adapt like a warrior, not like someone looking for shortcuts.

Above all, have fun. Become the warrior stepping into the cold, forging strength in the dark, preparing for the bulk season where monsters are made and muscle becomes armor. This program is your hunt — and your preparation for the forge that follows.
